correctness.rationale: The shortest-edge-chain metric is derived by endpoint minimization, with separate same-direction and cross-direction formulas. On each fixed coordinate direction, Walsh characters give the exact tensor-product eigenvalue; cross-direction coefficients give one real symmetric constant-diagonal block per Walsh subset. This supplies all d*2^(d-1) independent modes and verifies both spectral formulas with their multiplicities. For 0<z<1 all P_s are positive; the M_s factorization shows M_0 is the unique least transverse eigenvalue and gives a single sharp crossing and d-1-dimensional nullspace. Differentiation at z=1 gives the four-level ordinary distance spectrum. The embedded self-contained rational checker independently builds line-graph BFS distances, proves 30368 finite exact assertions on their Fourier action and traces, and brackets the root; the finite checks are explicitly distinguished from the analytic all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The central claim is the exact all-order exponential shortest-path kernel spectrum and its unique positive-semidefinite cutoff on the line graphs of Boolean cubes, not a Laplacian or adjacency-spectrum formula. Liu et al. prove Laplacian/resistance formulas for the same graph, Hou and Bian derive adjacency spectra, and Aalipour et al. derive ordinary distance spectra for other graph families. Neither those inspected statements nor the generalized distance-spectrum framework of DeVille supplies the claimed directional Fourier blocks or exact cutoff. Actual semantically matched published research records and recoverable prior claims yielded related but non-implying results. Unindexed equivalent historical coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent statement under an unindexed older name for the edge graph of the hypercube or a specialized Bose–Mesner algebra may exist.

Results on other generalized distance kernels may imply a subset of the present spectrum by additional computations not supplied in those sources; no independent exhaustive literature certification is claimed.

value.rationale: An unweighted cube line graph is a canonical infinite symmetric graph family with N=d*2^(d-1) vertices. Exact positivity thresholds for exponentially transformed shortest-path distances determine admissible kernel scales used in harmonic and metric spectral analysis. The Fourier eigenspace and d-1 rank drop locate the precise mechanism of failure, including the golden-ratio endpoint for the cuboctahedron and logarithmic growth of the threshold. This is a complete structural classification, not a reparametrization of a known adjacency spectrum or an arbitrary finite table; it is meaningful even though the metric is not of negative type for every d>=3.
